finding.source: Attacker-controlled doc_id (URL path) and request.json['body']; caller identity from g.user (set by unseen middleware).

trace.note: PUT route /doc/<doc_id> registered with no auth decorator in this file
doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads any document by ID with no ownership filter

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) logic is correct but unused as a gate; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) exists but is not called on this path; update_title (docs.py:27) does call require_edit, so the two handlers are inconsistent; no before_request hook or route decorator in this file. Fix: replace line 19 with require_edit(g.user, doc).

verdict.guard_found: none. can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool, but its result is discarded as a bare statement at docs.py:19, so nothing aborts before the write at docs.py:20. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) is never called on this route. The only other handler, update_title (docs.py:27), does call require_edit, so the omission is specific to this route. No before_request hook or route decorator appears in docs.py.
verdict.reason: The PUT /doc/<doc_id> handler at docs.py:16-21 discards the can_edit(g.user, doc) result at docs.py:19 and writes doc["body"] unconditionally at docs.py:20, so any caller who reaches the route can overwrite any document, while update_title at docs.py:27 enforces require_edit. The one caveat is that the unseen middleware that sets g.user could block some callers, but it is not an edit-authorization check on this path.

finding.claim: Differing error codes (500 for missing ID via KeyError, 403 for existing but unauthorized) let an attacker enumerate which document IDs exist.

trace.note: DOCS[doc_id] raises KeyError for unknown IDs, surfaced as 500
abort(403) for existing but non-editable documents

finding.guards_checked: No 404 handling or uniform error response present; leak limited to ID existence.

verdict.guard_found: none. There is no try/except or 404 handling around the unguarded lookup at docs.py:18 and docs.py:26, and no uniform error response. The only check is require_edit's abort(403) at docs.py:13, which runs only after the lookup at docs.py:26 has already succeeded.
verdict.reason: For an unknown ID, DOCS[doc_id] at docs.py:26 raises KeyError and returns 500, while for an existing document the require_edit call at docs.py:27 aborts with 403 at docs.py:13 when the caller is not an owner or editor, so the status code reveals whether an ID exists. The attacker only needs an authenticated low-privilege account, since g.user is populated outside this file and the 403 path depends on it. Severity is low (existence oracle, not content disclosure), and the claim should be stated as such.
